main_topics.reason: The user opened with severe nausea after the weekly dose and returned to ways to manage it throughout the conversation.
The user initially asked whether to quit, then explored alternatives because the medicine was helping their joints and asked whether to continue until the appointment.
The user asked whether taking folic acid on the same day as methotrexate was a problem and agreed to change the timing.
The user asked whether injections could reduce nausea, expressed fear of self-injection, and checked whether simpler options could come first.
The user asked whether an anti-nausea medicine could be taken safely with methotrexate.
The user asked what to tell the doctor and said they would write down the suggested points.

output.summary: The user described severe nausea after weekly methotrexate, which was helping their joints, and asked whether they could stop. The assistant discussed folic acid timing, splitting the dose, injections, and anti-nausea medication; the user felt reassured, planned small changes, and accepted a list to take to the doctor in two weeks.
